react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (reactome+smpdb+kegg+wikipathways) returned Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496) and Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150, SMPDB:SMP00068) as the top-ranked hits with FDR of 1.0e-15, driven by five input metabolites (testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, dihydrotestosterone, estrone) overlapping a 12-27 member pathway roster. The m/z-direct Mummichog algorithm independently recovered the same biological theme — C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) and Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) — with 13/13 and 12/12 input compound overlaps respectively, confirming that mass-network topology independently resolves the same five steroids as pathway members. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) with the same five-steroid hit set. The five non-steroid metabolites (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) did not enrich any pathway, suggesting they are peripheral or pharmacologically interfering species. Spironolactone is a known competitive antagonist of the androgen receptor and inhibitor of CYP17A1 — its presence alongside canonical steroid intermediates implies the treatment perturbed androgen-synthesis enzymes and/or steroid receptor occupancy. Dehydroepiandrosterone and androstenedione sit at the biosynthetic entry points of the pathway; testosterone and dihydrotestosterone represent downstream androgen-effectors; estrone anchors the aromatization arm converting androgens to estrogens.
